Compute the divergence between two context trees

Source: R/compare.R
tree_distance.Rd

tree_distance() computes the divergence between two context trees fitted to different sets of sequences, a measure of how differently they predict the next state. The distance is the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the two trees' next-state distributions (symmetric by default), computed for every context present in either tree and averaged with weights equal to the context's combined count in the two trees. A context missing from one tree is evaluated there at its longest fitted suffix, which is the distribution that tree would use for prediction. The value is 0 when the two trees predict identically and grows as their predictions separate.

It returns the distance only, in nats. It has no reference distribution, and it is positive even for two samples of one process; use compare_trees() for a permutation test and a per-context breakdown, or compare_groups() for more than two groups.

Usage

tree_distance(tree_a, tree_b, symmetric = TRUE)

Arguments

tree_a, tree_b

transitiontrees objects with the same alphabet.

symmetric

TRUE (default) for the symmetric divergence \(\frac{1}{2}(D_{KL}(A \| B) + D_{KL}(B \| A))\); FALSE for \(D_{KL}(A \| B)\) alone.

Value

A single non-negative number, in nats. It is Inf when, at a context with a positive count, one tree gives probability zero to a next state that the other tree gives positive probability.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input

(error) either argument is not a transitiontrees object.

transitiontrees_alphabet_mismatch

(error) the two trees have different alphabets.

See also

compare_trees() for the permutation test; compare_groups() for several groups.

Examples

high <- context_tree(subset(group_regulation_long, Achiever == "High"),
                     actor = "Actor", time = "Time", action = "Action",
                     max_depth = 2)
low  <- context_tree(subset(group_regulation_long, Achiever == "Low"),
                     actor = "Actor", time = "Time", action = "Action",
                     max_depth = 2)
tree_distance(high, low)
#> [1] 0.0705289
tree_distance(high, low, symmetric = FALSE)
#> [1] 0.06927832
